featured.name: Ngari, western Tibet (approx.)
featured.headline: Cold, dry Tibetan plateau block whose slopes and relief match Slater Plain.
featured.description: A 20 by 20 km block on the high plateau of western Tibet (Zanda to Gerze area), at 5,100 m elevation. Its slope histogram and relief track Slater Plain, and Landsat and Sentinel-2 imagery confirm the ground is mostly bare rock and sand. The place name is approximate: the block was found by terrain statistics, not by name, so check it on a map before quoting it.

featured.name: Mauna Kea, Hawaii (PISCES analog site)
featured.headline: Established lunar analog: basaltic volcano whose terrain scored 98th percentile against Mons Mouton.
featured.description: Mauna Kea hosts the PISCES lunar analog facility. We did not search for it: it is a validation check. Run through the same 40 m terrain pipeline, its 20 km block ranks in the 98th percentile of the discovery pool for match to Mons Mouton, which shows the engine can recognise a site people already use. Landsat classes 57 % of the block as vegetated, so the surface is far from bare.

featured.name: Atacama Desert, Yungay (Chile)
featured.headline: Hyperarid desert whose oxidising soils are a classic analog for Mars surface chemistry.
featured.description: The hyperarid core of the Atacama, around Yungay, is one of the driest places on Earth. Its soils have extremely low organic content and microbial activity, and are used as an analog for Mars's oxidising, dry regolith. The match is about surface chemistry and aridity rather than terrain: Yungay is flat, so it does not match the steep ground at Gale.
shortfalls: Much warmer and thicker air than Mars
Terrain is flatter than most Mars landing-site windows

references.title: Navarro-Gonzalez et al. 2003, Mars-like soils in the Atacama Desert, Chile, and the dry limit of microbial life. Science

featured.name: Lake Salda, Turkey
featured.headline: Alkaline lake with hydromagnesite shorelines, studied as an analog for Jezero's carbonates.
featured.description: Lake Salda in southwest Turkey is an alkaline lake with Mg-carbonate (hydromagnesite) deposits. It has been proposed as an analog for the Mg-rich carbonate seen from orbit at Jezero crater, the Perseverance landing site. The match is mineralogical and about a lake margin environment, not about terrain.

shortfalls: Wet, vegetated catchment unlike Mars

featured.name: Rio Tinto, Spain
featured.headline: Acidic, iron- and sulfate-rich river used as an analog for Meridiani's jarosite and hematite.
featured.description: The Rio Tinto in southwest Spain is an acidic, iron-rich river with sulfate minerals such as jarosite. It is used as an analog for the sulfate and hematite-bearing rocks that Opportunity found at Meridiani Planum. The match is about water chemistry and minerals, not terrain.
matches: Iron sulfates and oxides as at Meridiani
shortfalls: Biologically active; Mars is not known to be
Hillier than Meridiani's very flat plain

provenance.processing: Moon cards: three 'new' blocks and three reserves from results/v3_final_table.csv (composite across 10 categories, stability over 1,000 random re-weightings, distance to 166 catalogued sites, Landsat 8/9 and Sentinel-2 surface check). Values are the block's own values from earth_cells.json. 'Known' Moon cards (Mauna Kea, Wright Valley) are validation analogs. Mars cards are literature analogs unless a Mars Earth-match file was found. Place names are approximate; 'new' means at least 150 km from catalogued sites and nothing found in web searches only.
